idiom_name: sqlx query_as::<_, Row>() with #[derive(FromRow)] over an async pool
implementation_notes: sqlx is the async-first toolkit: PgPool/SqlitePool own the connections, query_as::<_, UserRow>("SELECT ... WHERE id = $1").bind(id).fetch_optional(&pool) maps rows into plain structs through #[derive(FromRow)], and the query!/query_as! macros verify the SQL against a live schema at compile time. The gateway is a thin type holding the pool with one method per statement. Prefer it for async services and when SQL should stay visible in the code but checked at build time.
pitfalls: A transaction borrowed from the pool and held across an .await in a single-threaded executor can deadlock; keep transactions short.
The compile-time macros need DATABASE_URL or a checked-in .sqlx offline cache, so an unconfigured CI fails to build rather than at runtime.
Decoding is type-strict: mapping a nullable column to a non-Option field fails only when the row is read.

variants.name: Diesel table! module with the compile-time query DSL
variants.idiom_name: diesel table! schema module (users::table) + insert_into/select returning Queryable structs
variants.implementation_notes: Diesel makes the gateway a compile-time module: table! { users (id) { id -> Int8, name -> Text } } is literally the table gateway declaration, insert_into(users::table).values(&new_row).execute(&mut conn) and users::table.find(id).first::<UserRow>(&mut conn) are the statements, and Queryable structs are the records. All column and type mismatches are compiler errors. Choose it when the schema is stable, sync execution is acceptable, and compile-time safety is worth generating schema.rs from the database.
pitfalls: Type or column mismatches surface as very large trait-bound errors; reading the 'required because' tail is a skill of its own.
schema.rs (diesel print-schema / migrations) must be regenerated after a migration or the DSL compiles against a stale schema.
The DSL covers only some SQL; complex reporting still needs diesel::sql_query, which drops the compile-time guarantees.
